title: Add benchmark-lab adaptive-batching reporting pipeline (v70)
author: Sofia Li
description: Motivation: adaptive batching has shown promising latency/cost tradeoffs in internal experiments. This PR wires an end-to-end reporting pipeline for the benchmark-lab to capture adaptive-batching experiments, ingest per-request batching metrics, and generate the v70 reporting artifacts used by analysis dashboards and downstream quality gates. Changes include a new pipeline config, representative workload runners adapted to produce variable inter-arrival patterns, a lightweight metric sanitizer for adaptive metrics, and dashboards/alerts to track regression risk. The goal is to make adaptive-batching experiments reproducible and visible in the same reporting flow as existing profiling baselines so teams can evaluate latency percentiles, throughput, and unit-cost tradeoffs across model variants. Checklist: - [x] Add pipeline orchestration manifest and schedules - [x] Implement representative runners for mixed arrivals and spike patterns - [x] Add metrics ingestion + sanitizer for batching-specific telemetry - [x] Wire reporting tables and summary aggregates used by dashboards - [x] Add basic dashboard and alert rules (can be iterated) - [x] Update docs and quickstart for running the v70 pipeline Notes: pipeline defaults to a non-destructive run frequency (weekly) and uses the benchmark-lab sandbox project. Operators can enable daily runs after initial validation. This PR is intentionally conservative about autoscaling test size to avoid capacity churn during rampup.
